verdict: Verisk grew revenue 5.3% to $809M on price increases across underwriting and claims, but a $17.5M investment loss and higher interest costs trimmed net income to $219M.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +5.3% YoY; +7.4% on an organic constant-currency basis

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: +5.6% YoY — buybacks shrank the share count

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: -40.5% YoY on collection timing and higher interest payments

segments.name: Underwriting
segments.note: Data, models and analytics insurers use to price and select risk — forms, rules and loss costs, plus catastrophe and risk solutions. Up 7.7% on an organic constant-currency basis.

segments.name: Claims
segments.note: Tools that help insurers handle claims — anti-fraud analytics, property estimating and restoration solutions.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs of running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Depreciation of fixed assets ($70M) plus amortization of intangible assets from acquisitions ($14M).

otherDetail: A $17.5M investment loss and $53.0M of net interest expense.

takeaways.title: Underlying growth is faster than it looks
takeaways.text: Reported revenue rose 5.3%, but on an organic constant-currency basis — stripping out currency and portfolio changes — growth was 7.4%, with subscription revenue up 8.2%.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS jumped 14%
takeaways.text: Diluted adjusted EPS rose 14.0% to $1.96, and GAAP EPS rose 5.6% to $1.70 — helped by buybacks, including a $100M accelerated repurchase in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Investments and interest cut net income
takeaways.text: Net income slipped 2.8% to $219M, mainly on a $17.5M investment loss and higher net interest expense, partly offset by operating leverage.

oneTimers: A $17.5M investment loss (mostly a $16.7M loss on cost-based investments), versus a $1.6M loss a year ago — the main reason net income fell despite revenue and EBITDA growth.
